coverage.note: Parametrized over all four classes. test_default_is_unlimited covers the None default, and the exact-limit and over-limit assertions cover the 413.
The middleware reads the chunked body itself. 10 bytes pass and 11 bytes give 413.

Parametrized over router, mount and route, with and without Content-Length. test_inner_limit_lowers_outer_limit covers lowering, and test_sibling_route_keeps_outer_limit checks the outer limit stays in force for other routes.
A tracked SpooledTemporaryFile is created before the limit is crossed. The test asserts one file was created and that it is closed after the 413.

findings.text: No test sends a lifespan or websocket scope through a limited Starlette, Router or Mount. The middleware passes non-http scopes through, but nothing here checks that the new wiring does not break them.
Router and Mount are only tested nested inside a Starlette app. A Router used directly as the ASGI app with max_body_size is not tested.
The new `self.max_body_size` public attribute is not required and is only read once, in build_middleware_stack. The `body_limit_middleware` temporary list could be folded into the stack expression.

summary: The wiring matches the plan, and each criterion has a test whose assertion would fail if the behaviour broke. I found no weakened tests: no existing test file was modified. I only read the code and did not run the tests. The remaining findings are advisory.
